$comment: Risk-tier rules. Engineer-owned: edits to this file are themselves red. Paths are repo-relative globs (** , *, {a,b}, leading ! excludes). 'added' is a regex tested against each added line. 'requireAny' flags a file whose final content contains none of the strings. 'block' denies the edit inside a Claude session for everyone; 'protected' denies it unless RISK_TIER_ROLE=engineer. CI re-checks everything regardless.

rules.why: Files like .env hold passwords and keys. They must never be saved into the project.
rules.next: Ask an engineer to add the secret to Cloudflare directly.

rules.why: This looks like a password or API key written into the code. Anyone who can see the code could use it.
rules.next: Remove it. Secrets are stored in Cloudflare by an engineer and read at runtime.

rules.why: This file controls the app's safety checks, infrastructure or ownership.
rules.next: Describe the change you want and an engineer will make it.

rules.why: This code decides who can use the app and blocks bots. A small mistake here can expose everything.
rules.next: Describe the change you want and an engineer will make it.

rules.why: This database change deletes, renames or rewrites existing data. That can't easily be undone.
rules.next: Only add new tables or columns. If existing data really must change, ask an engineer.

rules.why: This database step may already have run on the live app. Changing it now makes the live database and the code disagree.
rules.next: Leave it as it is and add a new migration instead.

rules.why: This stores information about real people (such as contact details, pay or health). Personal data has legal rules about who may see it and how long it is kept.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship will check who can see this data and how it is protected.

rules.why: This sends data to, or loads code from, a service outside the company (for example tracking scripts or another company's API).
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship will check what data leaves and whether we have an agreement with that service.

rules.why: This sends data to, or loads code from, a service outside the company (for example tracking scripts or another company's API).
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship will check what data leaves and whether we have an agreement with that service.
rules.$comment: Data code: any outside URL counts, however it is called (e.g. api = useRequestFetch(); api(url)).

rules.why: The app would send email. Emails reach real people and can't be taken back.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship will check who receives it and how sending is limited.

rules.why: This lets anyone on the internet save or change data, with no sign-in and no bot protection.
rules.next: Call requireUser(event) for signed-in staff, or verifyTurnstile(event, token) for a public form.

rules.why: This changes how the app is built or deployed. That is what keeps unreviewed code off the live app.
rules.next: Describe the change you want and an engineer will make it.

rules.why: This adds or changes a third-party library. Libraries run with full access to the app and its data.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship will check the library is trustworthy and maintained.
The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship checks which libraries changed and why.

rules.why: This changes how the app is built.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship checks the change is needed and safe.

rules.why: This changes what the app stores in its database.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship checks the new data looks right.

rules.why: This changes what the app's server does with data.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship checks it behaves as expected.

rules.why: An existing automatic check was changed or removed, so it might no longer check what was agreed.
rules.next: The engineer review at /yolo-sdlc:ship checks the examples still say what they approved.
